To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the serum levels of 5H5MI2CA and 5-S-cys-teinyldopa (CD) correlate with the weight of the highly pigmented B16 mouse melanomas.

the serum levels of 5(6) hydroxy-6(4) methoxyindole-2carboxylic acid (5H6 MI2C + 5H4MI2C) and 5S-cysteinydopa (5SCD) are good markers for the progression of melanoma, and that the accumulation of 5SCD in pigmented melanomas may be due to binding of this metabolite to melanin.
5H5MI2Cs and 5-S-Cys in serum may be better indicators of melanoma progression than their urinary excretion and that 5-S-CyS is accumulated in pigmented B16 tumors by virtue of binding with melanin.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new biochemical marker for melanoma progression.
the production, circulation, and urinary excretion of eumelanin and pheomelanin-related metabolite in B16 melanomas.
the production, circulation, and urinary excretion of melanoma metabolites in mice and the relationship between pigmentation and the production of these metabolites.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
5H5MI2CA + 6H6MI2CA, as well as 5-S- CD, are produced in melanoma and that their serum concentrations are correlated with tumor growth, whereas their urinary concentrations are not.
5-S-cys-tyl-Dopa and the 5(6)hydroxy-6-methoxyindole-2 carboxylic acids are both useful biochemical markers for monitoring the progression of melanoma.
the serum levels of 5H5MI2 and 5-S-CysD are better biochemical indicators than urinary levels for the evaluation of melanoma progression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the production of 5-S-OD in melanoma and the excretion in urine are not directly correlated, that 5H5MI2CA + 6H6MI2CA and 5-S-CDA are produced in highly pigmented melanoma and are excreted in urine, that 5-S-CDO is not produced in less pigmented melanoma, and that COMT plays a regulatory role in the accumulation of 5-S-COD in pigmented melanomas.

5H5MI2Cs and 5-S-cys are produced in the tumor tissue of B16 melanoma and excreted into serum and urine, respectively, in a similar pattern, suggesting that these metabolites may be used as biochemical markers of melanoma metastatic progression.
the production of 5H5MI2Cs, COMT activity, and 5-S-cysdopa production are all closely related to melanin biosynthesis in B16 melanomas.
The main takeaway from our work is that

serum levels of 5H5MI2Cs and 5-S-CysD are more closely correlated with the size of the tumor than the urinary levels of these compounds, and that the urinary levels of both 5H5MIs and 5-S-cysD are not significantly correlated with tumor size.
5H5MI2Cs may serve as a new biomarker for melanoma progression.
the urinary excretion rate of 5-S-CTD is not a good indicator of melanoma progression.
